text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for dedpool-jupiter-vpc: node gpu-4 reporting ECC_UNCORRECTABLE and rapid thermal climb >90C. Affected tenant: Aurelius Systems (dedicated pool). Auto-drain started but leases persisted. Paging on-call SRE.

pagerduty: Incident P-40432 created — Severity: P1. Initial impact: degraded inference latency and token failures for Aurelius in eu-west-2. Runbook: dedpool-gpu-fault -> isolate & replace node.

Henry (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Pulling logs + current routing. Who's owning customer comms?

Customer-Eng: Sam (account) and I are standing by. Sam: are we allowed to tell them we're performing a node drain/replace?

Sam (Account): Yes, tell them hardware fault in dedicated pool, isolating and migrating workloads. Do not promise ETA yet.

Maya (sre): Started remote drain: `sudo /usr/local/bin/dedpool-drain --node gpu-4 --force` — showing 18 active sessions, 12 of them are Aurelius. Beginning connection cutover to their fallback pool.

Liam (infra): Logs-Bot: pushed GPU telemetry. snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T09:22:13Z] gpu-4 ECC_UNCORRECTABLE count +1
[2026-03-14T09:22:14Z] thermal_zone0 temp 92.5C threshold 90
[2026-03-14T09:22:15Z] nvlink errors xfer drop
```

Logs-Bot: Also flagged a spot preemption window in the same host-group ~3m ago. Might be correlated.

Maya (sre): Eviction started for non-critical jobs. Progress: 7/18 sessions drained, 11 remain blocking due to long-running pinned KV-cache tasks.

Henry (oncall): Can we migrate pinned KV caches transparently? If not, spin warm replica and 302-route.

Liam (infra): KV-cache migration isn't instantaneous. Option: start warm replica on gpu-7 (same pool) and reroute new sessions. Kicking that now: `deploy-warm-replica --node gpu-7 --for-tenant Aurelius`.

Ops-Nina: Scheduling hardware replacement with cloud team. They're available in ~45m. If we can free the node sooner we can schedule earlier. I'll open hardware ticket.

Dmitri (hw): Noted. ECC + thermal often points to degraded VRAM or airflow. Capture `ipmitool sdr` and BMC logs before firmware changes. Also check firmware levels for sensor misreads.

Maya (sre): BMC dump excerpt pasted:
```
Sensor ID 07: GEM_TMP: 93 C -> CRITICAL
FRU: gpu-4
Power: stable
```

Henry (oncall): Customer impact status: token errors on 3 endpoints, elevated latencies on 6 routes. Degraded across models served from this pool. No total outage — fallbacks active but slower.

Customer-Eng: Sam: drafting message: "We're routing traffic away from the affected node and working on hardware replacement. Some requests may see increased latency. We'll update in 30 minutes." Good?

Sam (Account): Yep. Hold until we confirm replacement window.

Maya (sre): Drain progress: 12/18 drained. 6 still pinned (long-running interactive KV sessions). I'll force-evict two non-critical sessions after confirming owners.

Henry (oncall): Go ahead for non-critical. For anything marked 'Aurelius-critical' don't evict without account approval.

Maya (sre): Evicted 2 non-critical jobs. Now 4 remain: 3 Aurelius long-running, 1 internal eval.

Customer-Eng: Aurelius rep DM'd: long-running batch OK to restart; they'll accept restarts. Getting explicit ok.

Sam (Account): Aurelius approved restart of the batch. Proceed.

Maya (sre): Restarted those sessions on gpu-7. KV warmup in progress. Observability: ~50% of their traffic now hitting fallback. Latency improving.

Henry (oncall): Update incident status: Mitigating. Next: prevent regression from spot preemptions. Liam, can we pin critical Aurelius instances to reserved nodes?

Liam (infra): We can shard Aurelius critical traffic to reserved pool `rp-eu-west-2-a` — doing it now: `route-policy add --tenant Aurelius --pool rp-eu-west-2-a --priority high`.

Pagerduty: Note: manual mitigation applied by infra. Please annotate runbook.

Dmitri (hw): On hardware side: capture kernel OOPS and nvme logs. Also run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,Temperature` and attach.

Maya (sre): Pasting command outputs:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,Temperature
Ecc Errors (Volatile): 12
Ecc Errors (Aggregate): 1234
GPU Current Temp: 92 C
```

Ops-Nina: Hardware ticket created: HT-7741. ETA for swap: 32 minutes. Flagged expedited.

Henry (oncall): Customer message ready. Customer-Eng, drop it in channel once I confirm next-state stable.

Customer-Eng: Draft sent: "We detected a hardware issue in your dedicated pool node and have routed traffic to reserved capacity. We're replacing the node and expect normal performance to return within ~45 minutes. We'll keep you updated." They asked for a follow-up once replacement starts.

Maya (sre): Final drain status: 18/18 migrated or restarted. gpu-4 marked isolated. Triggered soft power cycle: `ipmitool chassis power cycle -p` -> BMC returned OK but sensors still report high temp. Keeping node isolated.

Liam (infra): Routing check: 100% of Aurelius traffic now on reserved pool. No token failures observed in last 3m. Trace: https://console.redwood/logs/trace/abc123

Logs-Bot: Alert: nvlink error rate dropping after migration; telemetry showing decreasing spikes.

Dmitri (hw): VRAM appears degraded. Recommend RMA and image replacement node with latest firmware. Coordinating with cloud ops on image.

Ops-Nina: Replacement scheduled in 28m. Cloud ops requested node remain isolated until new host ready.

Henry (oncall): Action items:
- Ops-Nina: coordinate physical replacement and RMA
- Dmitri: firmware image for replacement
- Liam: keep routing pinned to reserved pool until new node validated
- Maya: follow up on logs and close runbook
- Customer-Eng / Sam (Account): next update to customer in 30m

Maya (sre): I'll collect post-mortem notes. Quick datapoint: earlier spot preempt window may have accelerated thermal/IO stress; flag in postmortem.

Customer-Eng: Customer acknowledged message and satisfied with mitigation so far. They requested a post-incident writeup — Sam + Maya will own.

Henry (oncall): Handoff: I'm leaving incident to Maya for monitoring & postmortem. I'll be reachable if escalation. Handoff ack?

Maya (sre): Ack. Taking over active monitoring.

Dmitri (hw): I'll be on the swap call when ops-schedule starts.

Pagerduty: Incident status updated: Mitigated -> Maintaining. Please prefix all updates with `INC-40432`.

Henry (oncall): Closing my oncall loop. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Maya (sre): Will post final update when new node passes health checks and we reintroduce into pool. Current estimate: repair complete + validation in ~50m.

Customer-Eng: Noted. Scheduling postmortem with Aurelius for tomorrow and will include impact graphs.

Logs-Bot: Final telemetry snapshot will be archived to incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-40432/

Henry (oncall): End of thread for my shift. Good job.
